version.description:
Version is the capability's version, as a concrete version rather than a range: this is a
statement about what was installed, not a constraint on it.

Capability.description: Capability is one named, versioned capability the package contributes to the cluster.

namespace.description:
Namespace is the namespace it is deployed into. A requirement that names none is checked in
the engine's own default namespace: flux-system for fluxcd, argocd for argocd.

kind.description:
Kind is the workload's kind, Deployment when a requirement names none.

Two values, because those are the two a GitOps engine's components are: Flux's controllers
are all Deployments, and Argo CD's argocd-application-controller is a StatefulSet while the
rest of it is Deployments. A format that assumed Deployment would report Argo CD's single
most important component as absent on a healthy cluster.

version.description:
Version is a SemVer range the workload's own version must satisfy, read from the same
app.kubernetes.io/version label the engine sections are read from.

It is here so that a version can be required of something that is not a GitOps engine. A
package needing cert-manager v1.14, or an ingress controller new enough for an API it uses,
has no engine section to put that in -- and requiring an engine it does not use, purely to
get a version field, would be a prerequisite that refuses clusters for no reason.

Unconstrained when empty, which is the common case: most controller requirements are about
a workload being there and available at all.

minAvailable.description:
MinAvailable is how many replicas must report available. One is enough to reconcile; a
higher number is a statement about the package's tolerance for a controller restart during
its own deployment.

ControllerRequirement.description: ControllerRequirement is one workload that must be present and available.

version.description:
Version is a SemVer range the installed engine's version must satisfy, in that engine's own
numbering: a flux2 release for fluxcd, an Argo CD release for argocd.

It is read from the app.kubernetes.io/version label on the engine's own workloads, and
neither Flux's nor Argo CD's upstream manifests carry that label -- a package that vendors
them has to add it. A cluster whose engine carries no version label has the constraint
reported as unchecked rather than satisfied.

EngineRequirement.description: EngineRequirement requires a GitOps engine that is installed and new enough.

version.description:
Version is a SemVer range the API server's version must satisfy.

The examples are single comparators on purpose. A compound range like ">=1.30.0 <1.34.0"
is a legal value of this field and nothing here rejects one, but the only consumer that
exists -- the colonel_byte.zarf.prerequisites role -- reads one comparator and one version,
and records anything else as unevaluated rather than satisfied. Advertising a form that
reaches that consumer as a constraint it has to skip is advertising a check that does not
happen; see tasks/version_check.yml for why Jinja is not a semver library. The same applies
to EngineRequirement.Version and PackageRequirement.Version, which are the same comparison
over different data.

KubernetesRequirement.description: KubernetesRequirement constrains the cluster's own version.

package.description: Package is the zarf package's metadata.name, as written in its zarf.yaml.

version.description: Version is the zarf package's metadata.version.

description.description:
Description is a sentence saying what the package needs and why, for a human reading the
file rather than validating against it.

Metadata.description: Metadata names the package the document belongs to.

name.description: Name is the prerequisite package's metadata.name.

names.description:
Names are the metadata.name values that satisfy this requirement, any one of which will do.

It is how a requirement is stated for something that exists under more than one name: the
upstream init package reports itself as `init` and a rebuild of it as `init-slim`, and a
package needing an initialised cluster needs either. Several names rather than several
requirements, because the version constraint belongs to the requirement and not to each
name -- restating it per name is a constraint that gets bumped in one place and not the
other, which is how the two drift.

version.description:
Version is a SemVer range the deployed package's version must satisfy.

Under Names it applies to whichever of them the cluster has, and to each of them if the
cluster somehow has more than one.

PackageRequirement.description: PackageRequirement is one other Zarf package that must be deployed first, named either by the one name it has or by the several names it is published under.

capabilities.description:
Capabilities are named, versioned capabilities other packages may require. The name is a
label this format owns rather than anything Kubernetes knows about, which is what lets two
different packages provide the same capability -- `fluxcd-engine` from an upstream chart or
from a vendor's bundle.

crds.description: CRDs are the custom resource definitions the package establishes.

namespaces.description: Namespaces are the namespaces the package creates.

Provides.description: Provides is what the cluster becomes once the package is deployed: the half of the contract the packages downstream of this one require.

not.description: a package is reconciled by one GitOps engine, so requiring both is refused

kubernetes.description: Kubernetes constrains the cluster's own version.

fluxcd.description: FluxCD requires Flux, installed and new enough. Mutually exclusive with ArgoCD.

argocd.description: ArgoCD requires Argo CD, installed and new enough. Mutually exclusive with FluxCD.

controllers.description: Controllers are the workloads that must be present and available.

crds.description: CRDs are the custom resource definitions that must be established on the cluster.

storage.description: Storage requires somewhere for a PersistentVolumeClaim to land.

packages.description: Packages requires other Zarf packages to be deployed first.

Requires.description: Requires is the environmental prerequisites: what has to be true of the cluster before the package is deployed onto it.

defaultClass.description: DefaultClass requires the cluster to have a StorageClass marked as its default.

classes.description: Classes are StorageClasses that must exist by name.

accessModes.description:
AccessModes are the PersistentVolume access modes the package's claims ask for. A
single-node provider that offers only ReadWriteOnce is a prerequisite failure for a package
whose claims are ReadWriteMany, and it is one that surfaces as a Pending Pod rather than as
a deployment error.

StorageRequirement.description: StorageRequirement requires somewhere for a PersistentVolumeClaim to land.

metadata.description: Metadata names the package the document belongs to.

requires.description: Requires is what the cluster must already be, for this package to deploy onto it.

provides.description: Provides is what the cluster becomes once it has, for the packages that require it.

description: Document is a whole prerequisites document: the file a package ships as its `prerequisites` documentation key.
